To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) research in end of life care is difficult to conduct, but it is ethically desirable; (2) research in end-of-life care should be conducted in partnership with patients and families; (3) the outcomes that are most useful for research are also the ones most useful for clinical practice and should be short and responsive to change; (4) attrition is a normal feature of research in end of-life care and should be reported carefully using the MORECare classification system; and (
research evaluating services and treatment in end of life care should be: 1) mixed methods, 2) include patient and carer perspectives, 3) include economic evaluation, and 4) report attrition.

research in end of life care needs to: be designed and conducted in collaboration with patients and their families, use mixed methods, be conducted in the context of complex systems and include a wide range of outcomes, be designed and conducted to be responsive to attrition, include economic evaluation, and report in a way that is useful to all stakeholders.
In summary, our research is concerned with
how to do research in EoL care, not with the research itself.
how best to conduct research on the end of life and how to improve the care of patients at this time.
the quality and relevance of research in Eo LC.
